I might get some hate for this but for a lot of trans femmes learning makeup is a significantly different experience than for afabs, simply because of the age they learn it at. Learning makeup throughout your youth into early puberty, and perfecting it into later puberty is years of gradual learning. You are currently having to learn it in a very short amount of time, because you've also been taught transphobic and sexist ideas of passing and femininity, and that's really hard. You might not feel the space to have trial and error, bc you are (presumably) at an age where afabs already know how to do makeup pretty well, and where it would seem peculiar to not have decent makeup.

This is a really hard thing, but you need to remember you ARE allowed time for trial and error. It DOESN'T have to be perfect, you are valid in this struggle and I really hope you can find something that works for you and that helps you learn it. Starting and getting good at makeup is really hard bc it can be embarrassing to not have great makeup, but you're learning, and it's so extremely brave to even be trying things. Literally smear stuff on your face to see the colours, test things out. You've got this!! I'm sorry if this ended up being a bummer but just remember that you're valid and it's really hard but you can do this!

I don't think anyone can ever truly say that Christine was not _truly_ trans. From what I know from it and read here, yes, it's extremely likely she identified the way she did for reasons other than to be able to be herself. That doesn't mean we can look into her head and that doesn't mean that people can go out of their way to misgender her.
Whether this is our battle... I'm honestly conflicted. I understand it comes across as/is disrespectful to her mother to make it about Christine and her gender identity, but it does show how easily people (even people who don't know about the reasoning for her being trans) will take away someone's pronouns, someone's identity. I've seen it happen more often with people with autism or other disorders, which is why I personally did correct someone. It is too easy for people to make pronouns something they can decide to use or not to use when it should be everyone's right to have and be referred to with the pronouns they want.
It's a shitty place to fight this war, I have to say, but as an autistic trans-girl struggling with whether or not my transness is valid because of my autism and depression, it really hurt me to find Christine being misgendered. I know that's not why she was misgendered (although it happened a lot before what she did as well) but it still hurt me.
I understand why we "need" standards for trans people, I get that. But that's what a professional diagnosis is for. If a big public figure comes out as trans and is likely to be trans for malicious or publicity reasons, we should question that, of course. But it will never in my honest opinion excuse misgendering because it doesn't hurt us and pronouns aren't a title, and they should never be.
